questions.stem: What is the definition of potential difference?

options.text: The work done per unit charge (V = W/Q)
The total energy in a circuit
The rate of flow of charge

questions.explanation: Potential difference (voltage) is defined as the work done (energy transferred) per unit charge, given by V = W/Q. One volt means one joule of energy is transferred per coulomb of charge.

questions.stem: How should a voltmeter be connected to measure the potential difference across a resistor?

options.text: Between the resistor and the battery

questions.explanation: A voltmeter must be connected in parallel across the component to measure the potential difference between the two points on either side of it.

questions.stem: What is the difference between electromotive force (EMF) and potential difference?

options.text: There is no difference; they are the same thing
EMF is measured in watts while potential difference is measured in volts
EMF is the energy transferred per unit charge by the power supply, while p.d. is the energy transferred per unit charge by a component
EMF is always larger than potential difference in value

questions.explanation: EMF is the energy transferred per unit charge by the power supply (converting other forms of energy to electrical energy), while potential difference is the energy transferred per unit charge by a component (converting electrical energy to other forms).

questions.stem: In a series circuit with a 12 V battery, one resistor has a p.d. of 5 V across it. What is the p.d. across the other resistor?
questions.explanation: In a series circuit, the sum of the potential differences across all components equals the EMF of the battery (Kirchhoff's voltage law). Therefore 12 V = 5 V + V, giving V = 7 V.

questions.stem: In a parallel circuit, what can be said about the potential difference across each branch?

options.text: It is different for each branch and adds up to the supply voltage
It is zero in all branches
It is the same across each branch and equal to the supply voltage
It depends on the current in the branch

questions.explanation: In a parallel circuit, the potential difference across each branch is the same and equals the supply voltage. Each branch provides a separate path for current to flow.

questions.stem: A charge of 4 C passes through a component with a potential difference of 6 V across it. How much energy is transferred?
questions.explanation: Using V = W/Q rearranged to W = VQ: W = 6 V x 4 C = 24 J. The potential difference tells us the energy transferred per coulomb of charge.

questions.stem: Which equation correctly relates power, current, and potential difference?
questions.explanation: Electrical power equals current multiplied by potential difference: P = IV. This tells us the rate at which electrical energy is transferred by a component.
